question_text: Fill in: 'The official was accused ___ misconduct.'

hint_ladder.title: Idiom Check
hint_ladder.text: The verb 'accuse' is always paired with 'of' when specifying the wrongdoing. Think of 'accused of a crime'.

hint_ladder.title: Preposition Pairs
hint_ladder.text: Unlike 'charge with' or 'blame for', 'accuse' uniquely requires 'of'. Ang tamang partner ay 'of' lamang.

hint_ladder.title: Subukan sa sentence
hint_ladder.text: Fill the blank: 'The official was accused ___ misconduct.' Say it out loud: 'accused of misconduct' — ang natural pakinggan.

hint_ladder.title: Confirm Answer
hint_ladder.text: The only correct preposition is 'of'. Option C is the answer. Tandaan: 'of' after accuse, always.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'for' is used with 'blame for', but 'accuse' requires 'of'.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'with' pairs with 'charge', but 'accuse' takes 'of'.

C.text: Correct. 'Accused of' is the standard preposition.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'in' indicates location, but not the offense; the correct preposition is 'of'.

next_time_rule: Remember: 'accuse OF' (offense), 'charge WITH' (crime), 'blame FOR' (reason). Each verb has its own preposition.
deconstruct_text:
